Preferential retention of RRR-aT may also be the result of evolutionary selection of the fully methylated vitamin E analog form-
ing a more stable tocopheroxyl radical that upon full oxidation to alpha-tocopherol quinone/hydroquinone (aTQ/aTHQ) has non-
arylating electrophilic properties, whereas oxidation of bT, gT and dT leads to the arylating desmethyl analogs (bTQ, gTQ, dTQ)
with mutagenic, cytotoxic and apoptotic properties. Moreover, aTHQ may be the vitamin E analog with higher activity to prevent
ferroptosis and neurodegenerative dysfunction that occurs in the brain during vitamin E deﬁciency, by reducing the non-heme iron
of 15-lipoxygenase from its active Fe3þ to an inactive Fe2þ state.
Whereas intake of vitamin E is generally regarded as safe (RDA for humans is 15 mg/day, supplements are usually between 200
and 400 mg/day, and the upper tolerable limit is 1000 mg/day), adverse effects have been reported to occur above 400 mg/day
